title: Boundary-unit factorization in a regular local ring
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], hence Noetherian, and let $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ be members at distinct positions of a regular system of parameters of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters], with $r\ge0$. Then $A$ is an integral domain with unique factorization: every nonzero element is a unit times a finite product of prime elements, uniquely up to order and association. Each $t_i$ is prime. Put $T=t_1\cdots t_r$, with empty product $1$, and write $A[1/T]$ for localization at the powers of $T$. An element $f\in A$ becomes a unit in $A[1/T]$ if and only if $f=u\prod_{i=1}^r t_i^{a_i}$ for a unit $u\in A^\times$ and integers $a_i\ge0$.

source.place: Tag 0AG0, lemma-regular-local-UFD (lines 36800–36858): a regular local ring is a UFD; its proof first explains that a member of a regular parameter system is prime. The localization-unit clause is the elementary consequence of unique factorization detailed in report.md, rather than an assertion of the normal-crossings equivalence lemma.
